newsitem.title: USA: Perry says Iraqi troops still moving south.
newsitem.headline: Perry says Iraqi troops still moving south.

text.p: The United States sees "positive developments in northern Iraq" as Iraqi troops withdraw from the area, but continues to watch the situation closely, U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Friday.

"The latest information we have is that the mechanized and the armoured forces of the Iraqi troops have been pulling to the south," Perry told reporters. "The artillery shelling of Charchamal has stopped. Generally, we see positive developments in northern Iraq."

Last weekend's incursion by Iraqi troops into northern Iraq and their attack against Arbil triggered U.S. cruise missile strikes against Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's air defences in southern Iraq this week.

The United States has refused to rule out further attacks against Saddam, who says Baghdad will no longer recognise no-fly zones policed by the United States and its allies in northern and southern Iraq.

"So far, so good," Perry said during a Pentagon photo opportunity with visiting Argentine Defence Minister Jorge Dominguez when asked if the United States was satisfied with Saddam's withdrawal from the north.
"But I do not want want to be complacent about this at all. We are watching very, very carefully and we will base our future actions on what Saddam Hussein does."
